title: Jeanie Olham and the decision to go to Juilliard
summary: A schoolgirl, Jeanie Olham, told him about Juilliard. Rising to master sergeant, he decided not to stay in the Army and later enrolled.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So, I caught up with her and I said, “Hi, how are you doing?” I became aggressive, “What’s you name.” “Jeanie Olham.” Boy, what a strange name. I thought, I’d accept that beautiful girl and I could see that she’s very intelligent. I said that I have to appear intelligent. So I said, “You’re starting to graduate now, what are you going to be doing with your life?” She says, “I’m going to Juilliard.” I had never heard

of Juilliard. She saw that and she said, “Oh, Juilliard is the best music school in the country.” I said, “Oh, thank you.” I mention this because when I went to the Army and things started to look up and I’m starting to improve as a musician, I started getting right. There was a war officer who tested everybody, and he thought I was the best in the band. The next thing, I went corporal to buck sergeant, to this then ultimately master sergeant. So, but do you want your life to say you spent 20 years in the Army and retired. I said, “No.” I said, “You were a big fish in a little pond, but you better get out of here now or you’re going to be stuck.” I made it very clear, “Hey guys, bye, I’ve had it. You’ve got it!” “What are you going to do?” I said, “I’m going to Juilliard.” [It was] only because this girl had mentioned it. I went to Juilliard and it was one of the best things I ever did. I’ve never seen that girl since. I always wanted to give that girl a call, “Jeanie, did you ever go to Julliard? Because you sent me!”
